questions.question: Compare the uses of Mirror Stereoscope and Pocket Stereoscope.
questions.solution_html:
• Definition (1 mark): Instruments used to view overlapping aerial photographs in 3D.
  • Mirror stereoscope (2 marks): Uses mirrors and prisms; provides a wider viewing area and
  • supports detailed interpretation.
  • Pocket stereoscope (2 marks): Uses two lenses; portable, inexpensive and suitable for quick
  • observations.
  • Comparison (2 marks): Mirror type is larger and suited to detailed work; pocket type is
  • compact with a limited viewing area.
  • Conclusion (1 mark): Both are useful in photogrammetry and terrain interpretation.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: • Conclusion – : Both are useful in photogrammetry and terrain interpretation.

questions.question: Describe Overlay Analysis. Explain its importance in GIS-based spatial analysis.
questions.solution_html:
• Map Projection and Types (8 Marks)
  • Definition (2 marks): Mathematical transformation of the curved Earth onto a flat map
  • inevitably introducing distortions.
  • Cylindrical projection (1.5 marks): Uses a cylinder; useful for world maps and navigation.
  • Conical projection (1.5 marks): Uses a cone; suitable for middle-latitude regions.
  • Azimuthal projection (1.5 marks): Uses a plane; useful for polar regions and directional
  • mapping.
  • Properties and applications (1.5 marks): Conformal preserves angles, equal-area preserves
  • area, and equidistant preserves selected distances.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: area, and equidistant preserves selected distances.

questions.question: Explain the role of GIS in disaster management.
questions.solution_html:
• Overlay Analysis in GIS (8 Marks)
  • Definition (2 marks): Combines multiple spatial layers to identify relationships and patterns.
  • Types (2 marks): Vector overlay, raster overlay and weighted overlay.
  • Procedure (1 mark): Prepare datasets, align coordinate systems, select layers and perform
  • overlay.
  • Applications (2 marks): Site selection, groundwater potential, landslide zonation and land
  • use planning.
  • Limitations and conclusion (1 mark): Accuracy depends on input data quality, resolution and
  • appropriate weighting.

questions.question: Describe the basic principles of GPS. Discuss its major components and applications in geospatial studies.
questions.solution_html:
• Introduction (1 mark): GPS is a satellite-based positioning, navigation and timing system.
  • Basic principles (3 marks): Satellite signals, travel-time measurement, trilateration and use of
  • at least four satellites for standard 3D positioning with clock correction.
  • o Space segment (1 mark)
  • o Control segment (1 mark)
  • o User segment (1 mark)
  • Applications (4 marks): Surveying, GIS mapping, geological mapping, remote sensing
  • disaster management, precision agriculture and crustal deformation monitoring.
  • Conclusion and limitations (1 mark): GPS improves spatial data collection; atmospheric
  • errors, multipath and signal obstruction can reduce accuracy.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: errors, multipath and signal obstruction can reduce accuracy.
